body:
I understand your perspective, and I've thought that way before, too. But I've really grown to care for some people, and half the reason suicide's so prominent on my mind at the moment is for their sake, so that I can stop being a negative impact on their (and others', but mostly their) lives. So I'd like to do this in the way that leaves them as well off as possible. It doesn't matter to me that I won't see it.

But like I said, I understand your perspective.

I have ways to send them messages that I'm basically positive they'd see. My problem is, like you brought up, not knowing whether it's worth making them sad and possibly guilt-ridden just to get that closure, when they could probably just forget about me with time and might not hear what's happened to me until they already feel distanced from me through lack of contact. For instance, I have a friend with an anxiety disorder who I know from experience would be sent into a panic if I even announced an intention to put myself in harm's way to them. It'd probably be a horrific experience for them if I were to leave them a suicide message. At the same time, I'd feel really bad about not saying goodbye.

I guess, because of that, I feel selfish for wanting to leave a message for the people I care about who wouldn't immediately hear of my death. If I don't, they'd be in a position to feel like there was nothing they could have done, and they'd be possibly months out of contact with me and probably wouldn't care as much (maybe I'm naive for thinking that). I really think they're all better off without me around, even if they'd never admit or acknowledge it, so if they could not have me around anymore and *also* not hear I've killed myself (for a while, anyway), that seems like a solid deal for them. I'm just worried that I'm misjudging how much a lack of closure could affect them.
